title: India Wins Four Gold Medals at 58th International Chemistry Olympiad in Tashkent
excerpt: All four Indian students secured gold medals in a historic sweep at the IChO 2026 in Uzbekistan, marking India's best-ever performance at the competition
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India achieved a historic clean sweep, winning four gold medals at the 58th IChO in Tashkent.
  • This performance marks India's best-ever result at the International Chemistry Olympiad.
  • The competition featured 363 students from 92 countries, with 41 gold medals awarded.
  • Three Indian gold medalists were trained at the ALLEN coaching institute in Kota, Rajasthan.
  • India's previous average was 1.3 gold medals per edition over the last decade.

  • All four Indian students — Kabeer Chhillar, Harshit Singla, Sandeep Kuchi, and Debadatta Priyadarshi — won gold medals at the 58th IChO in Tashkent
  • This is India's best-ever performance at the International Chemistry Olympiad, with a perfect 4-out-of-4 gold medal haul
  • The competition featured 363 students from 92 countries, with 41 gold medals awarded overall
  • Three of the four Indian gold medalists were trained at the ALLEN coaching institute in Kota, Rajasthan

India has delivered its finest-ever showing at the International Chemistry Olympiad, with all four members of its team winning gold medals at the 58th edition of the competition held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, from July 10 to 19, 2026.

The Indian gold medalists and their ranks among 363 competitors from 92 countries are: Kabeer Chhillar (Rank 26), Harshit Singla (Rank 35), Sandeep Kuchi (Rank 37), and Debadatta Priyadarshi (Rank 39), according to official results published on the IChO website.

A Historic Clean Sweep

The four-gold haul represents a significant leap from India's previous performances. At the 57th IChO in Dubai in 2025, India secured two gold and two silver medals. Over the past decade, India had averaged roughly 1.3 gold medals per edition according to cumulative IChO statistics. The 2026 result is the first time India has achieved a clean sweep of gold medals at the chemistry olympiad.

The 58th IChO awarded 41 gold, 74 silver, and 112 bronze medals. China's team topped the individual rankings with four students in the top five, while teams from the United States, Vietnam, Chinese Taipei, and Singapore also performed strongly.

The Indian Team

Three of India's four gold medalists — Harshit Singla, Kabeer Chhillar, and Debadatta Priyadarshi — were students at the ALLEN coaching institute, which announced their selection for the national team in April 2026. Sandeep Kuchi, a returning olympiad veteran from Hyderabad, also competed at the 57th IChO in 2025, where he won gold at Rank 25.

Debadatta Priyadarshi, from Bhubaneswar, Odisha, similarly returned from the 2025 team where he had earned a silver medal at Rank 75 — making his 2026 gold a dramatic improvement of 36 places in the overall rankings.

"This achievement is a matter of pride not only for the institute but for the entire country." — ALLEN coaching institute, on its students' selection for the IChO 2026 team

The Road to Tashkent

India's IChO team is selected through a rigorous multi-stage process coordinated by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE), a national centre of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR). Students must clear the National Standard Examination in Chemistry (NSEC), the Indian National Chemistry Olympiad (INChO), and an intensive Orientation-cum-Selection Camp (OCSC) before being named to the four-member team.

The competition itself consists of a five-hour theoretical examination worth 60 percent of the total marks and a five-hour practical laboratory examination worth 40 percent. Gold medals are awarded to the top 10 to 12 percent of all competitors.

India's Growing Olympiad Strength

The Tashkent result adds to a banner year for India in international science olympiads. Earlier in July 2026, India's five-member team at the 56th International Physics Olympiad in Bucaramanga, Colombia, won five gold medals and jointly achieved the world number-one rank — another historic first.

India's science olympiad programme is supported by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the Department of Space (DOS), and the Ministry of Education, under the umbrella of the National Steering Committee on Science Olympiads.

Diaspora Connections

India's olympiad success resonates deeply within the global Indian diaspora, where STEM education remains a cornerstone of community identity. Coaching networks, alumni mentorship, and diaspora-funded scholarship programs have increasingly contributed to the pipeline that feeds India's olympiad teams. The results also reinforce India's reputation as a source of world-class scientific talent — a narrative that carries weight in university admissions and hiring across the United States, United Kingdom, and other countries with large Indian-origin populations.

What's Next

The 59th International Chemistry Olympiad in 2027 will be hosted by Chinese Taipei. With back-to-back gold-heavy performances in 2025 and 2026, India will enter that competition with rising expectations and a new generation of chemistry talent eager to build on the Tashkent triumph.
